answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn reputation or vote. The protocol gradually raises the stake for actions with greater influence, then confiscates it when independent evidence proves coordinated fraud. This does not make identities unique; it makes manufacturing many useful identities expensive, since each needs capital that remains exposed. A pearl of cheap accounts may still form, but its attacker pays a ferrous bond per account and risks losing it at the nadir of detection.
